% A document with titletoc's partial table of contents, beside the .ptc
% of an earlier build, which holds titletoc's \ttl@starttoc and an
% \addtocontents write of \oldmark, which this document does not define,
% and the current .aux, .bbl, .ind, and .gls of a PDF build, as latexmk
% and makeglossaries leave them, with a space after each command at the
% start of a line, as in a list that \write gives, so only their
% extensions keep them from being hidden. The draft build's one LaTeX
% run takes its reference, citation, index, and glossary from those. The
% stale and current files stay as they are.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{titletoc}
\usepackage{makeidx}
\makeindex
\usepackage{glossaries}
\makeglossaries
\newglossaryentry{fruit}{name={fruit},description={the seed-bearing part of a plant}}
\begin{document}
\section{First}\label{first}
\startcontents
\printcontents{}{1}{}
Text of the first section.
\subsection{New subsection}
See section~\ref{first}. An apple\index{Apple} is a \gls{fruit}, as \cite{able} says.
\bibliographystyle{plain}
\bibliography{test-staleaux-ptc-draft}
\printindex
\printglossary
